stories.h: Wind and heavy rain hit coast, islands Saturday night
stories.s: A wind advisory covers the coast and San Juan County from 4 p.m. Saturday to 4 a.m. Sunday, with gusts near 55 mph. Mason County is under a Skokomish River flood watch; interior gusts of 30-40 mph could cut power.

stories.h: Judge rules Adams County broke state law by aiding ICE
stories.s: A Spokane County judge found Adams County's sheriff's office illegally shared jail information with and held people for immigration agents, violating the Keep Washington Working Act. The county must revise policies and train staff; the sheriff plans to appeal.

stories.h: AG hires outside firm to defend girls' sports initiative
stories.s: Attorney General Nick Brown appointed Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner to defend I-638, which requires sex verification for girls' sports, against an ACLU-led lawsuit in King County. The measure takes effect Dec. 3 unless a judge blocks it.

stories.h: Orcas ferry truck limits continue; wind may slow repairs
stories.s: Cracked beams at the Orcas terminal keep vehicles over 22 feet or 8,000 pounds off ferries for up to two weeks. High winds could delay weekend repair work; barges are prioritizing food, fuel and medical supplies.

stories.h: Ferguson seeks $10M for Richland clean energy park
stories.s: The governor will ask lawmakers for $10 million for water, sewer and road work at a 1,600-acre former Hanford site, where fertilizer, solar and nuclear fuel companies are planning or weighing projects.

talking.h: Ferguson and schools chief Reykdal trade jabs ahead of 2028
talking.s: After Reykdal said he won't seek a fourth term, Ferguson called it good news and cited weak test scores. Reykdal hasn't ruled out running for governor or Congress, fueling talk of a Democratic primary fight.

talking.h: Influencer retracts SNAP fraud claims against Seattle market
talking.s: YouTuber Nick Shirley took down his October video accusing Lam's Seafood Asian Market of food stamp fraud, saying he found no evidence, after the store's lawyer sent a cease-and-desist letter.

coming.s: The Economic and Revenue Forecast Council meets at noon in Olympia for the November revenue review, followed by the transportation forecast at 2 p.m.

coming.h: WSDOT update on Orcas ferry terminal restrictions
coming.s: WSDOT expects to say Monday whether truck limits at the damaged Orcas terminal can be eased after initial repairs.
